persians.label: verified
persians.says: The Persians sacked Athens in 480 BC and destroyed the temples on the hill.
quote: The Older Parthenon was still under construction when the Persians invaded and sacked the city in 480 BC.
to rebuild the sanctuaries that had been destroyed by the Persians

pericles.label: verified
pericles.says: After victory over the Persians, Athens rebuilt the hill in the 5th century BC under Pericles.
quote: In the 5th century BC, the Athenians, empowered from their victory over the Persians, carried out an ambitious building programme under the leadership of the great statesman Perikles

propylaia.label: verified
propylaia.says: The Propylaia gateway, by Mnesikles, was built from 437 to 432 BC.
quote: Built between 437 and 432 BC as a part of the Periklean Building Program
the Propylaia by Mnesikles (437-432)

unfinished.label: supported
unfinished.says: The Propylaia was abandoned unfinished in 432 BC, with its lifting bosses still on the blocks.
quote: the project was abandoned in an unfinished state in 432 with the lifting bosses remaining

nike.label: disputed
nike.says: The temple of Athena Nike is dated to 427-424 BC by UNESCO and to around 420 BC by other sources.
quote: the Temple of Athena Nike by Mnesikles and Kallikrates (427-424)
was finished around 420 BC

nike-small.label: supported
nike-small.says: The temple of Athena Nike is the smallest temple on the Acropolis.
quote: The Temple of Athena Nike, the smallest on the Acropolis

parthenon-dates.label: verified
parthenon-dates.says: The Parthenon was built between 447 and 438 BC; its decoration went on until 432 BC.
quote: Built between 447 and 438 BC
work on the artwork and decorations continued until 432 BC.

architects.label: verified
architects.says: The Parthenon is attributed to the architects Iktinos and Kallikrates, with the sculptor Pheidias supervising.
quote: It is attributed to the architects Iktinos and Kallikrates, with the general supervision of the work and responsibility for the sculptural programme in the hands of the sculptor Pheidias.

curve.label: supported
curve.says: The Parthenon floor bulges upward at the centre by 10.3 cm over 70 m.
quote: the stylobate is curved, bulging upward at the centre—by 10.3 cm over 70 m

entasis.label: supported
quote: the columns exhibit entasis, i.e., swelling that reduces toward the top

curve-why.label: disputed
curve-why.says: Scholars propose several explanations for the curves.
quote: Scholars have proposed several explanations for the curvatures found in Parthenon.

athena-gold.label: supported
athena-gold.says: Thucydides reports Pericles saying the Athena statue held forty talents of pure gold that could serve as a reserve.
quote: According to Thucydides, during the Peloponnesian War when Sparta's forces were first preparing to invade Attica, Pericles, in an address to the Athenian people, said that the statue could be used as a gold reserve if that was necessary to preserve Athens, stressing that it "contained forty talents of pure gold and it was all removable"

church-date.label: disputed
church-date.says: The Greek Ministry of Culture dates the conversion to a church to the fifth century AD, first to Saint Sophia and later to the Virgin Mary; Wikipedia also gives the final decade of the 6th century.
quote: until the fifth century AD, when it was converted into a church dedicated first to Saint Sophia and later to the Panagia (Virgin Mary)
In the final decade of the 6th century AD, the Parthenon was converted into a Christian church dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

church-name.label: supported
church-name.says: Medieval Greek accounts call it the Temple of Theotokos Atheniotissa.
quote: In medieval Greek accounts it is called the Temple of Theotokos Atheniotissa

latin.label: supported
latin.says: Under the Latin occupation it was a Catholic church of Our Lady for about 250 years.
quote: At the time of the Latin occupation, it became for about 250 years a Latin Catholic church of Our Lady.

ottoman.label: disputed
ottoman.says: The Ottomans took the Acropolis in 1458 by one account, 1460 by another; the Parthenon became a mosque before the end of the fifteenth century.
quote: until June 1458, when it surrendered to the Turks
the taking of Athens by the Turks in 1460
Some time before the end of the fifteenth century, the Parthenon became a mosque.

mosque-why.label: disputed
mosque-why.says: Exactly how it became a mosque is unclear.
quote: The precise circumstances under which the Turks appropriated it for use as a mosque are unclear

explosion.label: supported
explosion.says: On 26 September 1687 a Venetian mortar round blew up the gunpowder the Ottomans stored in the Parthenon.
quote: used the Parthenon as a gunpowder magazine
On 26 September 1687 a Venetian mortar round, fired from the Hill of Philopappos, blew up the magazine.

explosion-why.label: disputed
explosion-why.says: Accounts conflict on whether the hit was deliberate.
quote: Accounts written at the time conflict over whether this destruction was deliberate or accidental

elgin.label: supported
elgin.says: From 1801 to 1812 agents of Lord Elgin removed about half the surviving Parthenon sculptures and sent them to Britain.
quote: From 1801 to 1812, Elgin's agents removed about half the surviving Parthenon sculptures

elgin-legal.label: disputed
elgin-legal.says: The legality of the removal is disputed.
quote: The legality of Elgin's actions has been disputed.

restoration.label: verified
restoration.says: The restoration work running today began in 1975.
quote: an integrated intervention begun in 1975 and continues today

caryatid-london.label: supported
caryatid-london.says: One of the Caryatids ended up in the British Museum.
quote: This is how one of the caryatids was separated from the rest of the building and ended up in the British Museum.

olive.label: legend
olive.says: Athenians pointed to a sacred olive of Athena and trident marks of Poseidon at the Erechtheion.
quote: the sacred olive tree of Athena would have been
indentations below were thought to be the resulting trident marks

contest.label: legend
contest.says: The west pediment showed Athena and Poseidon disputing for possession of Athens.
quote: the west pediment showed Athena and Poseidon disputing for the possession of the city of Athens before the gods

statue.label: verified
statue.says: Inside stood Pheidias's gold and ivory statue of Athena Parthenos.
quote: the sculptor Pheidias supervised the entire building program and conceived the temple's sculptural decoration and chryselephantine statue of Athena
a background for the gold and ivory statue of Athena Parthenos

paul-where.label: disputed
paul-where.says: It is unclear whether Paul spoke on the hill itself or before the council, which probably met elsewhere by then.
quote: it is unclear whether Paul gave his speech before the Areopagus Council
The Areopagus Council likely would not have met on the actual Areopagus hill by the time of Paul's visit

mosque-gone.label: supported
mosque-gone.says: The small mosque in the Parthenon was demolished in 1843.
quote: The Parthenon mosque was demolished in 1843

parts.name: Arrival
parts.stand: Stand just past the ticket gate at the west entrance, to the side of the path, where you can look up at the gateway of columns.

paras.t: Here we are, at the foot of the Acropolis. Take a breath before the climb.

Almost everything you'll see up top was built in one burst of confidence. In 480 BC the Persians sacked Athens and destroyed the temples on this hill. After the Greeks won that war, the city rebuilt it all under the statesman Pericles.
Two practical things before we climb. Take the marble steps slowly and watch your footing. And carry water with you.

parts.name: The gateway
parts.stand: Stop inside the gateway, between the big columns.

paras.t: This gateway is the Propylaia, designed by the architect Mnesikles and built from 437 to 432 BC.
Here's something most people walk straight past. The Propylaia was never finished. Work stopped in 432 BC, with the builders' lifting bosses still left on the blocks.

Look up to your right at the little temple on its own bastion. That's the temple of Athena Nike, Athena of Victory, the smallest temple on the hill. Its date isn't settled: UNESCO gives 427 to 424 BC, other sources say it was finished around 420 BC.

parts.name: The Parthenon
parts.stand: Walk through the gateway onto the open rock and stop where you see the west end of the Parthenon at an angle.

paras.t: And there it is. The Parthenon, the temple of Athena, protector of the city. It was begun in 447 BC and completed in 438 BC, with the carving going on until 432. The architects were Iktinos and Kallikrates, and the sculptor Pheidias was in charge of the sculpture.

Now here's the secret of this building. It looks perfectly straight, but it isn't. The floor bulges upward in the middle, about 10 centimetres over 70 metres. The columns swell slightly too. Scholars still argue about exactly why the builders did it.

Picture it whole. Inside stood the statue of Athena by Pheidias, in gold and ivory. According to the historian Thucydides, Pericles told the Athenians it held forty talents of pure gold, a reserve the city could use in an emergency.

parts.name: The Parthenon's other lives
parts.stand: Stay beside the Parthenon, anywhere along its long side.

paras.t: Here's the part of the story most visitors never hear. For a very long time this was a church. It became a church, first of Saint Sophia, Holy Wisdom, and later of the Virgin Mary. The Greek Ministry of Culture says that happened in the fifth century AD; other sources say the late 500s, so the sources differ. Medieval Greeks called it the church of the Theotokos Atheniotissa, Our Lady of Athens.

Then came Latin crusader lords, and for about 250 years it was a Catholic church of Our Lady. The Ottomans took the hill in 1458, or 1460 by another account, and before the end of that century the Parthenon was a mosque. Exactly how that happened is unclear.

Then came the worst day in its history. On 26 September 1687 a Venetian army was bombarding the hill. The Ottomans were storing gunpowder inside the Parthenon. A mortar round hit, and the middle of the building blew apart. Accounts from the time disagree on whether the gunners meant to hit it.

More was lost later. From 1801 to 1812, agents of the British ambassador, Lord Elgin, removed about half the surviving sculptures and sent them to Britain. Whether that was legal is still disputed, and Greece has asked for them back.
The cranes you see are the restoration teams. Their current work began in 1975, and it's still going.

parts.name: The Erechtheion and the Maidens
parts.stand: Cross to the north side and face the porch held up by six statues of young women.

paras.t: This is the Erechtheion, and these are the Maidens, the Caryatids, carrying the roof on their heads. One of the original Maidens ended up in the British Museum in London.

This is also where Athens kept its founding legend. As the story goes, Athena and Poseidon competed for the city, a contest carved on the west end of the Parthenon. It's legend, not history, but Athenians pointed to a sacred olive of Athena here, and to marks in the rock said to be from Poseidon's trident.

parts.name: Closing
parts.stand: On your way back down, at the top of the gateway steps.

paras.t: Take one last look back. A temple, a treasury, a church of the Virgin Mary, a mosque, a gunpowder store, then a ruin, and now a building that people are patiently putting back together. Every age has found something here worth saving.

Below the entrance is a bare rocky hill, the Areopagus. The book of Acts links it to the apostle Paul's speech to the Athenians, although historians aren't sure whether he spoke on the hill itself or before the council named after it.

practical.t: Hours, tickets and closures change with the season and the weather. Check the official ticket site before you go.
